newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rostelekom says doubles authorised capital.
newsitem.headline: Rostelekom says doubles authorised capital.

text.p: Russian long distance telecoms company Rostelekom shareholders have voted in a postal ballot to double company capital by authorising almost one billion ordinary shares, a company securities department official said on Thursday.

"Yes, they definitely approved authorised shares in the amount of the existing capital," the official said. The move is not a new share issue. A company official had said previously the board would seek shareholder approval before a new issue.

The official said 933,750,400 ordinary shares had been authorised for issue at the discretion of the board of directors. Previously company capital was 700,312,800 ordinary shares and 233,437,600 prefs.

Shareholders are not required to give further approval to issue new 2.5 rouble par value shares, but securities department head Igor Kochezhkov said in July Rostelekom had no issue plans and would not make an issue without shareholder approval.
Foreign shareholders have about 30 percent of Rostelekom, one of the most liquid shares on the Russian market. Svyazinvest holding company has a controlling 38 percent stake.
Shareholders were required to postmark the mail-in ballot which replaced an annual meeting by July 18 and 75 percent of shareholders were required to approve the charter change.
